newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends with short covering gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends with short covering gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures mostly ended higher Thursday in a fairly active session, lifted by short covering, particularly in May, before it went off the board, industry sources said.
May climbed 6.2 cents to expire at $2.122 per million British thermal units. June settled 4.5 cents higher at $2.122. Most others ended steady to up by 3.7 cents.

"We were under pressure all day. May was brought up on short covering, but I think June outpaced itself and I'd like to sell it," said one East Coast trader, noting cash in most regions tumbled more than a dime today.
Despite today's gains, some expected pressure when May flows begin, citing comfortable storage levels and the prospect for milder spring weather next month.
Temperatures in the Northeast and Midwest were expected to moderate to near-normal levels by the weekend.
Technical traders pegged important support in June at $2.03 and then along the short-term up trendline in the $2.00 area. Resistance was seen at $2.24 and then in the $2.33 area.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices skidded more than 10 cents Thursday to the $2.05-10 area. Midcontinent pipes were down a similar amount to the mid-$1.90s. Gas at New York city gate also stumbled more than 10 cents to the $2.35-40 range.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 2.7 cents to $2.211.

On the KCBT, May finished one-half cents higher at $1.955, while deferreds ended up by one to two cents. The East/West spread widened by 5.7 cents to 16.7 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 661 lots changed hands, up from Wednesday's total of 596.
KCBT May natgas expires Friday, April 25.
